title: How was your weekend?
goal: Tell people what you did. Bulgarian has two simple past tenses; this unit teaches the one you need nine times out of ten — the **aorist**, the form for completed events.
bekal: forming the past tense for all three verb groups
noticing that the "you" and "he/she" forms are exactly the same
telling the story of a day gone by

dialogs.title: Диалог — Monday morning on campus
dialogs.intro: Ivan asks about Ani's weekend. Notice that the form for *ти* and for *той* is exactly the same — and that it is never confusing, because the sentence always makes it clear.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Great! On Saturday I went to Vitosha.
lines.literal: very — good! on — Saturday — I-went — to — Vitosha.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: No, with Maria. We left early and came back at six.
lines.literal: no, with — Maria. we-set-off — early — and — ourselves — we-returned — at — six.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Very much. I saw the whole city from above.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: On Sunday I did nothing. I slept till noon, read and watched a film.
lines.literal: on — Sunday — not — I-did — nothing. I-slept — until — noon, I-read — and — I-watched — film.

lines.speaker: Иван:
lines.id: I worked all day. I wrote two tests.
lines.literal: I — I-worked — whole — day. I-wrote — two — tests.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: You poor thing! Working the whole weekend.

lines.speaker: Иван:
lines.id: It's fine. Next week I'll rest.
lines.literal: nothing — at-all. next-the — week — will — I-rest.

notes: ⚠️ **The form for ти and for той/тя/то is exactly the same**, in every verb group. *Ти работи* and *Той работи* look identical in the past. This is no flaw in the language; context always makes it clear, and you can add the pronoun if needed. English past tense doesn't mark the person either: "you worked", "he worked".

⚠️ **Watch the stress shift.** The past often moves the stress to another syllable: *работя* (*ra-BO-tya*) → *работих* (*ra-BO-teeh*), but *чета* (*cheh-TA*) → *четох* (*CHEH-toh*). The stress of the past form almost always falls further forward than in the present.

**Bulgarian has TWO simple past tenses, and this book teaches one.** The one taught here is the **aorist** — a completed event, seen as one whole. The one not taught is the **imperfect**, which describes something ongoing at the time: *четох* (I read it to the end) versus *четях* (I was reading). At A1, the aorist covers almost everything you need.
**Спах, четох, видях are past forms to learn as a whole.** Verbs with a short, irregular present are usually irregular in the past too. The full list is on the next page.
**Цял ден means "all day"**, and *цял* follows gender: *цял ден*, *цяла седмица*, *цяло лято*, *цели дни*. Notice again the я/е switch you saw in *голям / големи*.

**Горкият literally means "the poor one" and is used just like "you poor thing" in English.** For a woman it is *горката*, for several people *горките*. It can stand alone as a full sentence of sympathy.

**Хареса ли ти? — "did you like it?"** The structure is reversed: the subject is **the thing that is liked**, and the person is the receiver. Unit 17 is all about this pattern, so for now just learn it as a whole.

**Написах, not писах.** The prefix **на-** shows that the job is finished — the tests got done. *Писах* means "I wrote" without saying whether it was finished. Pairs like this exist for almost every Bulgarian verb and are the main topic of level A2.

grammars.title: Aorist — the past tense for completed events
body: The pattern is the same in every group: add **-х** for *аз*, nothing for *ти* and *той*, then **-хме / -хте / -ха** for the plural. All that differs between groups is the linking vowel.
after: The linking vowel can be **-и-**, **-а-**, **-о-** or **-я-**, and it can't always be guessed from the present. The safest way: learn the **аз** form of every new verb, and the whole table follows by itself.
The negative just adds **не** in front, as usual: *не работих*, *не отидох*, *не бях*.

grammars.title: The twenty most common past forms
body: The *аз* form and the *ти/той* form, because those are the two you will say most often.
after: ⚠️ The four most often confused: **взех** (not *вземах*), **дойдох** (not *идвах*), **видях** (not *виждах*), and **казах** (not *казвах*). The forms in brackets exist, but they are imperfect — the other past tense, which you haven't learned yet.

blocks.text: **Преди means "before" and also "… ago".** *Преди два дни* (two days ago), *преди една година* (a year ago), *преди обяд* (before lunch). The pattern is always *преди* + the period of time.
⚠️ **Снощи means "last night", not the night before that.** And *вчера вечерта* means the same thing. Both are common.

sections.title: Telling the story of a day — a pattern you can copy

blocks.text: Read the short story below out loud, then write your own version about yesterday. Six sentences are enough; what matters is getting the past forms right.

head: Bulgarian
English
rows: Yesterday I got up at seven.
I had breakfast and went to school.
На обед ядох баница и пих кафе.
At noon I ate banitsa and drank coffee.
In the afternoon I read and wrote exercises.
Вечерта гледах филм и си легнах рано.
In the evening I watched a film and went to bed early.

blocks.text: Notice that the pronoun doesn't appear even once. The ending **-х** already shows the subject is "I", so adding *аз* to every sentence actually makes the story sound stiff.

blocks.title: ⚠️ The costliest mistake in this unit
items: When you speak fast, it is tempting to let the **time word** carry the past and grab the first verb form you know — the present: "yesterday" seems to do the job on its own.
That instinct produces Bulgarian sentences like *Вчера отивам на Витоша* — a past time word with a present verb. It isn't just informal; it sounds wrong, like "yesterday I go".
The drill is simple and must be practiced until it's automatic: **every time you say вчера, снощи or миналата седмица, check your verb ending.**

vocab.en: long ago, for a long time

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right past form.
Put the words in the right order.

items: Yesterday I got up at seven.

answers: Работих цял ден. — Ти чете книгата. — Тя отиде на море. — Ние бяхме в София. — Те спаха до обед. — Видях приятеля си.
Как мина уикендът? — В събота отидох на Витоша. — Тръгнахме рано и се върнахме. — Не правих нищо. — Работих цял ден.
Вчера станах в седем. — Тръгнахме рано. — Не правих нищо. — Хареса ли ти? — Работих цял ден.
